answer: The ledge multiplier is published, charged in lantern, and anchor lists each payment. A burst of registrations therefore prices itself out, since the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. The admission burn is multiplied by 3 for each identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. A farm of 2120 identities would post 4878 proofs and burn roughly 60 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
